mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected upward crossing of the unemployment rate above 9.7% triggers a loss of labor market confidence, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods where UNRATE crosses above 9.7% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices signals a robust economic expansion, reducing uncertainty and boosting equity valuations, which translates to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods with rising GDPC1 and INDPRO are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, lowering long-term interest rates and enhancing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansion periods with FEDFUNDS < 2.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in labor demand (PAYEMS) above 1.5 million indicates strong job market activity, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in periods where PAYEMS crosses above 1.5M are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a recessionary environment, a sustained drop in the supply index (INDPRO) below 95 signals weak business activity and reduced investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in recessionary periods with INDPRO < 95 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month rise in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods of rising FEDFUNDS are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices over the next 60 days reflects a robust economic expansion, reducing uncertainty and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in periods with rising GDPC1 and INDPRO are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
